text: Official event information presents PUBG Asia Stars as a six-region Asia event centered on PUBG streamers, creative modes and scheduled live broadcasts.
Day 1 is held. The later controversy centers on Himass and TanVuu receiving and allegedly using information from outside normal gameplay.

The two Vietnamese players publish apologies. The meaning of those apologies becomes disputed: Korean-side accounts say they expected an explicit admission of stream sniping, while the posted text did not contain such an admission.
Team Korea boycotts Day 2 in protest over tournament management and handling of the controversy.
A rulebook revision is publicly archived. A complete before/after version comparison remains necessary.
KRAFTON cancels remaining matches and continues evidence review, including match video, participant POV material and team voice materials.
The event fallout expands: reporting documents sponsor/promotional pauses while KRAFTON's response is awaited.
ChosunBiz reports that Asia Stars lacked mandatory stream-delay and live-chat restrictions that are used in some ordinary PUBG competitions.

KRAFTON publishes its investigation result, permanently banning Himass and TanVuu from PUBG accounts and official PUBG esports while also acknowledging operational responsibility and an internal review.
GAM x TE challenges proportionality; Anyone's Legend says it is reviewing rules, procedures and instructions to support Himass's appeal rights.
